name: 德西德里乌斯·伊拉斯谟

points.title: 早年生活
points.description: 伊拉斯谟于1466年出生于鹿特丹的一个私生子家庭。他的父亲是神父，母亲是医生的女儿。尽管家庭背景复杂，但伊拉斯谟接受了良好的基础教育，在德文特和斯海尔托亨博斯的学校学习拉丁语和古典文学。这段时期的教育为他后来的学术成就奠定了基础，也培养了他对古典文化的热爱和对教会腐败的早期批判意识。
points.descriptionEn: Erasmus was born in 1466 in Rotterdam as an illegitimate child. His father was a priest and his mother was the daughter of a physician. Despite his complex family background, Erasmus received a good education, learning Latin and classical literature at schools in Deventer and 's-Hertogenbosch. This period of education laid the foundation for his later academic achievements and cultivated his early love for classical culture and his critical awareness of church corruption.

points.title: 修道院生活
points.description: 1485年，伊拉斯谟进入斯泰恩的奥古斯丁修道院，成为一名修士。这段经历让他深入了解了教会的内部运作，也使他开始质疑修道院生活的某些方面。在修道院期间，他继续学习神学和古典文学，并开始创作一些早期的文学作品。这段经历塑造了他后来对宗教改革的温和立场，他既希望改革教会，又反对马丁·路德激进的做法。
points.descriptionEn: In 1485, Erasmus entered the Augustinian monastery at Stein, becoming a monk. This experience allowed him to gain deep insight into the internal workings of the Church and led him to question certain aspects of monastic life. During his time in the monastery, he continued to study theology and classical literature and began writing some of his early literary works. This period shaped his later moderate stance on the Reformation, as he desired to reform the Church while opposing Martin Luther's radical approach.

points.title: 巴黎求学
points.description: 1495年，伊拉斯谟前往巴黎大学深造，这是当时欧洲最重要的学术中心之一。在巴黎，他专注于神学研究，同时也深入研读了古希腊和罗马的经典著作。这一时期，他开始形成自己的人文主义思想，强调通过古典学习和理性思考来改革教会和社会。1503年，他获得神学博士学位，并开始在巴黎教授神学。巴黎的学习经历极大地拓展了他的学术视野，为他后来的学术生涯奠定了基础。
points.descriptionEn: In 1495, Erasmus went to the University of Paris for further studies, one of Europe's most important academic centers at the time. In Paris, he focused on theological studies while also deeply studying the works of ancient Greek and Roman classics. During this period, he began to form his own humanist ideas, emphasizing the reform of the Church and society through classical learning and rational thinking. In 1503, he received his doctorate in theology and began teaching theology in Paris. His studies in Paris greatly expanded his academic horizons and laid the foundation for his later academic career.

points.title: 意大利人文主义
points.description: 1506年至1509年，伊拉斯谟首次访问意大利，在都灵、博洛尼亚和罗马等地游历。这次旅行使他接触到意大利文艺复兴的人文主义思想，特别是洛伦佐·瓦拉的著作对他的影响深远。1509年，他创作了《愚人颂》，这部讽刺作品批判了教会的腐败和世俗权力的愚蠢，成为他最著名的作品之一。1514年至1515年，他再次访问意大利，在威尼斯和罗马等地停留。意大利的经历极大地丰富了他的思想，使他成为北欧人文主义运动的重要代表人物。
points.descriptionEn: From 1506 to 1509, Erasmus made his first visit to Italy, traveling through Turin, Bologna, and Rome. This trip exposed him to Italian Renaissance humanist ideas, particularly the works of Lorenzo Valla, which had a profound impact on him. In 1509, he wrote 'The Praise of Folly,' a satirical work that criticized the corruption of the Church and the folly of secular power, becoming one of his most famous works. From 1514 to 1515, he visited Italy again, staying in Venice and Rome. His experiences in Italy greatly enriched his thinking and established him as a leading figure in the Northern Renaissance humanist movement.

points.title: 晚年与学术巅峰
points.description: 1521年，伊拉斯谟定居瑞士巴塞尔，这里成为他晚年生活和学术创作的中心。在巴塞尔期间，他完成了大量重要著作，包括《新约圣经》的希腊文与拉丁文对照版（1516年出版，在巴塞尔修订再版），这部作品对宗教改革产生了深远影响。他还创作了《基督教骑士手册》、《论自由意志》等重要作品。在宗教改革期间，他采取温和立场，既批评教会的腐败，又反对马丁·路德的激进观点。1536年，伊拉斯谟在巴塞尔去世，他的思想和作品对欧洲人文主义和宗教改革产生了持久影响。
points.descriptionEn: In 1521, Erasmus settled in Basel, Switzerland, which became the center of his later life and academic work. During his time in Basel, he completed numerous important works, including the Greek-Latin parallel edition of the New Testament (first published in 1516, revised and republished in Basel), which had a profound impact on the Reformation. He also wrote significant works such as 'The Handbook of the Christian Knight' and 'On Free Will.' During the Reformation, he adopted a moderate stance, criticizing the corruption of the Church while opposing Martin Luther's radical views. Erasmus died in Basel in 1536, and his ideas and works had a lasting influence on European humanism and the Reformation.

supporter.zh: 伊拉斯谟被誉为'北欧文艺复兴的王子'和'基督教人文主义之父'。他通过批判性思维和古典学习，推动了欧洲思想解放，为宗教改革奠定了理性基础。他的《新约圣经》修订工作促进了圣经研究的科学化，而《愚人颂》则成为讽刺文学的经典。伊拉斯谟提倡温和改革，主张通过教育和道德修养而非暴力变革来改善社会，这种思想对后世的人文主义和启蒙运动产生了深远影响。
supporter.en: Erasmus is hailed as the 'Prince of the Northern Renaissance' and the 'Father of Christian Humanism.' Through critical thinking and classical learning, he promoted the liberation of European thought and laid a rational foundation for the Reformation. His revision of the New Testament advanced the scientific study of scripture, while 'The Praise of Folly' became a classic of satirical literature. Erasmus advocated for moderate reform, believing in improving society through education and moral cultivation rather than violent change, an idea that profoundly influenced later humanism and the Enlightenment.

critic.zh: 批评者认为伊拉斯谟过于保守，未能彻底解决教会腐败问题，反而延缓了必要的改革。他的温和立场被指责为妥协和机会主义，特别是在面对宗教改革的关键时刻。一些宗教改革家如马丁·路德批评他缺乏勇气，未能坚定地站出来反对教会的弊端。此外，伊拉斯谟的学术方法也受到质疑，他过度依赖古典文本而忽视当代现实问题，被认为脱离了当时的社会政治现实。
critic.en: Critics argue that Erasmus was too conservative, failing to thoroughly address the corruption of the Church and instead delaying necessary reforms. His moderate stance has been criticized as compromising and opportunistic, particularly at the critical moment of the Reformation. Some reformers like Martin Luther accused him of lacking courage in firmly opposing the Church's abuses. Additionally, Erasmus's academic methods were questioned for his over-reliance on classical texts while neglecting contemporary real-world issues, seen as detached from the social and political realities of his time.

objective.zh: 历史学界普遍认为伊拉斯谟是连接中世纪与近代思想的关键人物。他既保留了基督教传统，又引入了人文主义的新思想，成为欧洲思想转型的重要桥梁。在流行文化中，伊拉斯谟常被描绘为理性与温和改革的象征，与激进的宗教改革家形成对比。他的思想影响了从托马斯·莫尔到伏尔泰的众多思想家，其作品至今仍是研究文艺复兴和宗教改革的重要文献。伊拉斯谟的生平体现了知识分子的社会责任与独立思考的重要性，成为后世学者的重要精神遗产。
objective.en: Historiography generally regards Erasmus as a key figure connecting medieval and modern thought. He preserved Christian traditions while introducing new humanist ideas, serving as an important bridge in Europe's intellectual transformation. In popular culture, Erasmus is often depicted as a symbol of rationality and moderate reform, contrasting with radical reformers. His ideas influenced numerous thinkers from Thomas More to Voltaire, and his works remain important sources for studying the Renaissance and Reformation. Erasmus's life exemplifies the importance of intellectual social responsibility and independent thinking, becoming a significant intellectual legacy for later scholars.

self.zh: 真正的自由不在于随心所欲，而在于能够掌控自己的欲望。
self.en: True freedom is not the ability to do whatever you want, but the ability to control your own desires.

others.zh: 伊拉斯谟是欧洲最博学的人，他使整个欧洲都变得更有智慧。
others.en: Erasmus was the most learned man in Europe, he made the whole of Europe wiser.
